title: Alchemy and Impurities
titles: A Treatise on Alchemy and Toxicity
text:
Excess or unrelated elemental Qi increases impurity. For a required score, excess starts above the target plus the larger of 10 or 25% of that target.


Cultivation recipes use their non-neutral total for this allowance. Unrequested non-neutral elements count as impurity in elemental recipes.


The impurity fraction is the excess/unrelated score divided by the total ingredient score, capped at 1.


If neutral is not a required ingredient, the ideal neutral base is 10% of the recipe's required score, with a minimum of 10.


Amounts from 75% to 125% of that ideal give the full bonus: up to 5 purity points and 3 percentage points less failure risk. Smaller amounts give a partial bonus.


Above 125%, the bonus falls, reaching zero at twice the ideal; the excess above 125% also counts as impurity.


Required neutral ingredients, such as Bigu's base, do not grant this optional bonus.


Successful purity (%) is 95 - 50 x impurity fraction + 5 x neutral bonus, rounded to a whole number and limited to 1-100. Purity describes the result; it is not a guarantee of success.


A successful pill with purity of 70% or less leaves one alchemy remnant for each complete 10% of lost purity: 70% yields 3, 60% yields 4. Leave two output slots free for the pill and waste.


A ruined batch produces 10 remnants.


With this knowledge and the recipe, the cauldron preview shows an estimated purity range. Failure and Recipe Difficulty explains the separate failure roll.
